successors.name: Dahomey
successors.text: Allada, conquered by Dahomey in March 1724; 'Dahomey permitted the existence of a subordinate royalty'

ledger.x: 12th or 13th century: Aja migrants from Tado found Allada.

c. 1600: the brothers split the Aja kingdom. 'until c. 1600, when three brothers - Kokpon, Do-Aklin, and Te-Agdanlin - split the rule of the region amongst themselves'; Do-Aklin founds Dahomey on the Abomey Plateau.
c. 1600: Te-Agdanlin's share becomes Little Ardra / Ajatche (Porto-Novo). The Porto-Novo page has Te-Agbalin's group reach the region of Ajashe 'in the late 16th century'.
1724 (March): the independent Kingdom of Allada ends.

wars.name: Dahomean conquest of Allada
wars.outcome: Dahomey won in March 1724: thousands slaughtered in three days, more than 8,000 captured and sold; a subordinate royalty allowed.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the shape is the Atlantique department less Whydah, a stand-in.
